claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic structure.
As-cast TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
As-cast TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K and approximately 30% strain.
High-energy ball milling followed by SPS can produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion of 0.5–1 vol% Y2O3 in TiVNbTa.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain thermally stable in TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede dislocation motion in the BCC matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will hinder dislocation glide and dynamic recovery at elevated temperature.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries in TiVNbTa.
Grain-boundary pinning by Y2O3 will retard grain coarsening at elevated temperature.
Oxide-particle strengthening and grain refinement can increase the strength of a BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Adding 0.5–1 vol% Y2O3 will raise the TiVNbTa yield strength above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding Y2O3 will improve compressive strength relative to as-cast TiVNbTa at 1273 K.
The Y2O3-strengthened alloy will maintain reasonable ductility at 1273 K.
Testing at 1273 K to approximately 30% compressive strain represents the relevant mechanical boundary condition for the proposed intermediate layer.
The proposed condition simulates service as a heat-transfer layer between W and CuCrZr.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts only a yield strength significantly or notably above 330 MPa, whereas the falsification rule effectively requires a greater-than-50% increase. An outcome between 330 and 495 MPa could satisfy the stated prediction yet be classified as falsification.

The experiment specifies an identically processed Y2O3-free control, but the decision rule compares the treated material primarily with the 330 MPa as-cast baseline rather than with that control, so it does not cleanly isolate the effect of Y2O3 from milling and SPS.
